Lentil Digital Twin Console

2–4 GHz free-space microwave moisture meter · archive replay (digital shadow) + virtual machine
What is this screen and how do I read it? (click to read)

No new measurements can be taken, so the archived records are sent to the twin one by one, in measurement order, as if they were arriving live from the machine.

For each record the twin predicts MC and compares bulk density obtained in two ways: weighing (ρg = mass / volume) and the microwave model (ρd, which does not use mass). If they disagree, the record is suspect and a repeat measurement is requested.

How to read it: the coloured box in the middle is the twin's latest decision (green = trusted, amber = suspect, red = unusable, blue = season calibration). The four boxes below show moisture, the density found in two ways and the score (z) of their difference. When z is around zero the machine looks healthy; above 3 the twin becomes suspicious. The charts show the same scores over time; the left panel shows the raw record from the machine, the right panel the twin's memory and the buttons you can press. The “Predicted vs true values” card puts the true values the twin never sees (oven MC, gravimetric density) next to the predictions.

The buttons on the right add synthetic faults (e.g. a 96 g weight on the platform). Responses to commands such as REPEAT are emulated from the archive by a virtual machine; they are not responses of the real machine.

Hover over or tap any term with a dotted underline to see what it means. The full list of symbols and terms is in the glossary at the bottom of the page (the "❓ Symbols" button takes you there).

3D machine view (schematic)

Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom. Beam, sample and displays update with every record.

Dimensions from the paper: 28 cm between antenna apertures, 20 × 20 × 24 cm sample volume, 3 cm Styrofoam walls. Horn, platform, front-end and PC shapes are schematic. Beam attenuation follows the record's mean ΔA, sample colour follows predicted MC, and the load-cell display shows the measured mass.
